content: Running time increases with input size, so we analyze algorithms by expressing time as a function of the input size. For example, sorting 6 elements is much faster than sorting \(6 \times 10^9\) elements. When analyzing running time, we usually care about upper bounds because they give users a guarantee that the program will not take more than a certain amount of time. Lower bounds are less useful for users because knowing a program takes at least a certain time does not tell you how long it might actually run.
